title: The mill, 1994 · pages 12–13
logline: The last shift. Everyone from the 1994 group photo, aged nothing. Gully's uncle with the shack's keys. The one sentence.

panels.composition: The mill floor on the last shift, 1994, drawn in the 2023 hand with Era I's black spotting brought back on purpose. The great saw. Twenty-odd workers in caps and suspenders, every face from a group photograph, none aged. Cedar dust hanging in the rafters as the page's only wash, a pale ochre. In the foreground, the one figure not from the photo: GULLY'S UNCLE, young, forty, holding a ring of keys — the shack's — looking at the saw. Hand-lettered below the spread, the only sentence in the private work: 'I was fourteen and I thought this was the end of something. It was the end of something. I just had the wrong something.'
panels.caption: I was fourteen and I thought this was the end of something. It was the end of something. I just had the wrong something.
